scenarios.title: Ransomware Attack on Corporate Network
scenarios.description: A ransomware attack has been detected. Navigate through the office to identify the source, contain the spread, and recover systems.

rooms.name: Reception Area
rooms.description: Main entrance with security desk and visitor logs

objects.name: Reception Computer
objects.description: The receptionist reports strange pop-ups appearing on their screen
objects.clue: Suspicious email attachment opened this morning

objects.name: Visitor Logbook
objects.description: Physical visitor log from the past week
objects.clue: A vendor visited IT department yesterday with USB drive

objects.name: Security Phone
objects.description: Direct line to security operations center
objects.clue: Alert received at 8:47 AM about unusual network activity

options.text: Isolate the reception computer immediately
options.feedback: Good - quick containment prevents spread

options.text: Check all computers in the building first
options.feedback: Too slow - ransomware spreads quickly

options.text: Call the IT help desk
options.feedback: Helpful but not urgent enough for active attack

objects.name: Main Server Rack
objects.description: Central server infrastructure showing encryption in progress
objects.clue: Ransomware is actively encrypting shared drives

objects.name: IT Admin Workstation
objects.clue: Attack originated from HR department workstation

objects.name: Backup External Drive
objects.description: Offline backup drive stored in safe
objects.clue: Last backup was 24 hours ago - data can be restored

decision_points.question: How do you contain the ransomware spread?

options.text: Disconnect all network cables immediately
options.feedback: Excellent - complete network isolation stops spread

options.text: Shut down servers only
options.feedback: Partial - workstations can still spread malware

options.text: Enable firewall rules to block traffic
options.feedback: Good but may be too late if already inside network

objects.name: HR Manager Workstation
objects.clue: Opened 'Invoice.zip' attachment from fake vendor email

objects.name: Employee Records Cabinet
objects.description: Physical backup of sensitive employee data
objects.clue: Contains PII that could be exposed in breach

decision_points.question: What forensic evidence should you collect?

options.text: Image the hard drive before shutdown
options.feedback: Perfect - preserves volatile memory and evidence

options.text: Just take screenshots of the screen
options.feedback: Insufficient - loses critical forensic data

options.text: Reinstall the OS immediately
options.feedback: Destroys all forensic evidence!

scenarios.title: Customer Data Breach Investigation
scenarios.description: Customer payment data has been exfiltrated. Investigate the breach, identify the vulnerability, and implement controls.

rooms.name: Company Lobby
rooms.description: Main entry point with visitor management

objects.name: Visitor Check-in Kiosk
objects.clue: Kiosk has unrestricted access to internal network

decision_points.question: How do you begin the breach investigation?

options.text: Review network logs for unusual traffic
options.feedback: Excellent - logs show data exfiltration pattern

options.text: Interview employees who handled customer data
options.feedback: Helpful but logs provide objective evidence first

options.text: Shut down all customer-facing systems
options.feedback: Disruptive and may destroy evidence

objects.name: Payment Database Server
objects.clue: SQL injection vulnerability detected in API endpoint

objects.name: Firewall Configuration
objects.clue: Outbound traffic to unknown IP addresses logged

decision_points.question: How do you address the SQL injection vulnerability?

options.text: Apply WAF rules immediately and patch code
options.feedback: Perfect - immediate protection while permanent fix develops

options.text: Take the payment system offline
options.feedback: Secure but impacts business operations

options.text: Schedule patch for next maintenance window
options.feedback: Too slow - active exploitation ongoing

scenarios.title: Insider Threat Detection
scenarios.description: An employee is suspected of stealing intellectual property. Navigate the office to gather evidence while maintaining confidentiality.

objects.name: Suspect's Workstation
objects.description: Employee's primary computer with monitoring software
objects.clue: Large file transfers detected after hours to personal cloud storage

objects.name: Unusual USB Drive
objects.description: External storage device found near workstation
objects.clue: Contains copies of proprietary source code

decision_points.question: How do you proceed with the investigation?

options.text: Discreetly monitor digital activity
options.feedback: Good - preserves evidence without alerting suspect

options.text: Confront the employee immediately
options.feedback: Premature - may destroy evidence or cause flight

options.text: Search their desk while they're away
options.feedback: May compromise investigation legally

rooms.name: Private Conference Room
rooms.description: Secure meeting space for investigation team

objects.name: Investigation Case Files
objects.clue: Timeline shows pattern of escalating data access

decision_points.question: When should you escalate this investigation?

options.text: Immediately to legal and HR leadership
options.feedback: Correct - insider threats require cross-functional response

options.text: After gathering more evidence yourself
options.feedback: Risk of investigation going too far without oversight

options.text: Only if you find definitive proof
options.feedback: Too late - damage may be irreparable
